fixes.title: Windows Update, BITS or CryptSvc service disabled
fixes.note: Restores the default start type of a disabled service (Manual for wuauserv and BITS, Automatic for CryptSvc). Nothing is forced to Automatic. Exits 1 if a policy keeps the service disabled.

fixes.title: Windows Update scan fails or update agent not responding
fixes.note: Restarts the update agent, renames SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 only when they look broken (nothing is deleted) and triggers a scan. Installation stays with your update rings.

fixes.title: Component store or system file corruption (DISM/SFC)
fixes.note: Runs DISM /RestoreHealth and sfc /scannow when the store is repairable. If a servicing restart is outstanding, the script waits: restart the device and run it again.

fixes.title: WSUS or GPO update policy conflicts with Intune/Autopatch
fixes.note: Removes WSUS and GPO update blocks. Skipped automatically on devices with a Configuration Manager client, where these values are set on purpose.

fixes.title: Latest quality update missing
fixes.note: There is no single script for this: a missing monthly update is a symptom. Fix the other patching findings in this report first, then check the update policy.
manualSteps: Fix the other patching findings in this report first (service disabled, scan failed, pending restart, low disk space, WSUS leftover): they are the usual cause
Intune: Devices > Windows > Update rings: is the device in a ring, are quality updates paused, how long is the deferral?
Autopatch: Tenant administration > Windows Autopatch > Devices: is the device registered, in a group and not 'Not ready'?
Intune > Reports > Windows updates (or Windows Update for Business reports): look up the device's error code
On the device: Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates, note the error code; Get-WindowsUpdateLog writes WindowsUpdate.log to the desktop
Last resort: install the current cumulative update by hand from the Microsoft Update Catalog

fixes.title: Feature update blocked (safeguard hold or setup error)
fixes.note: A safeguard hold is set by Microsoft on purpose because of a known compatibility issue. Fix the cause (usually a driver or app) instead of forcing the update.
manualSteps: Note the GatedBlockId from the report evidence
Look it up in Windows release health (Known issues of the target version) or in the Intune feature update report, which names the safeguard hold
Update the affected driver or app (often audio, display, Bluetooth or a specific app) from the OEM or Windows Update
Run the appraiser again: schtasks /run /tn "\Microsoft\Windows\Application Experience\Microsoft Compatibility Appraiser", then check again after a few hours
Only for test devices: Settings catalog > Windows Update for Business > Disable WUfB Safeguards
If setup itself fails: run SetupDiag and check its result

fixes.title: Reboot pending
fixes.note: No script needed. Never clear the pending-reboot registry keys.

fixes.title: Less than 20 GB free on C:
fixes.note: Cleans only caches Windows recreates: Delivery Optimization, Windows Temp and error reports older than 7 days, old update downloads, then DISM StartComponentCleanup (no ResetBase). User data, profiles, the recycle bin and Windows.old are not touched.
manualSteps: If the script is not enough: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files and Cleanup recommendations (shows the largest items per user)
Turn on OneDrive Files On-Demand and Storage Sense by Intune policy (Settings catalog > Storage / OneDrive)
Remove Windows.old only when no rollback is needed: Settings > System > Storage > Temporary files > Previous Windows installation(s)
Check for large user folders (Downloads, Videos, PST files) with the user before deleting anything

fixes.title: Disk errors or unhealthy physical disk
fixes.note: Diagnostic only. Escalate to hardware support; do not run repairs.

fixes.title: Diagnostic data disabled (no Autopatch/WUfB report data)
fixes.note: Removes a leftover Group Policy AllowTelemetry=0 (backed up first, skipped with a Configuration Manager client or -removePolicyBlocks 0) and sets DiagTrack back to Automatic. An Intune policy with AllowTelemetry=0 is only reported.
manualSteps: Intune: Settings catalog > System > Allow Telemetry = Required (or higher) for Autopatch devices
Remove any GPO that sets 'Allow Diagnostic Data' to 'Diagnostic data off' for these devices
Check that no debloat or privacy tool disables the DiagTrack service again

fixes.title: Required Microsoft endpoints not reachable
fixes.note: Direct TCP test: results are not reliable behind an explicit proxy.

fixes.title: Device not enrolled in Intune
fixes.note: Triggers automatic enrollment (GPO task or deviceenroller /AutoEnrollMDM) and reports the enrollment error code. Intune cannot run a remediation on an unenrolled device: run it as SYSTEM with psexec -s, ConfigMgr or a GPO task, with the user signed in. The report detail names the cause; fix that first if it is the join or the MDM scope.
manualSteps: Read the cause in the check detail: not Entra joined, no MDM URL, GPO missing, or an error code
Not Entra joined: fix AAD.PRT.MISSING or AAD.HYBRIDJOIN.PENDING first
No MDM URL: Entra admin center > Mobility (MDM and WIP) > Microsoft Intune > MDM user scope must include the user; check the Intune license
Hybrid joined without GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > MDM > Enable automatic MDM enrollment using default Azure AD credentials (User Credential)
0x80180018: assign an Intune license. 0x8018002B: verify the UPN domain or add the user to the MDM scope. 0x80180014: check enrollment restrictions (platform, personal devices)
Entra joined (cloud) without automatic enrollment: Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Enroll only in device management
Collect diagnostics: mdmdiagnosticstool.exe -area "DeviceEnrollment;DeviceProvisioning;Autopilot" -cab C:\Temp\mdm.cab

fixes.title: No successful Intune sync for 7 days
fixes.note: Enables disabled Intune sync tasks, sets dmwappushservice back to Manual and starts the PushLaunch task to trigger a sync. Missing sync tasks mean a damaged enrollment: see MDM.ENROLLMENT.BROKEN.
manualSteps: Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > your account > Info > Sync
Intune admin center > Devices > the device > Sync, then check the last check-in time
If sync still fails: Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider > Admin

fixes.title: MDM enrollment damaged or device certificate broken
fixes.note: Re-enrolling changes the device's management state, so it is a guided step, not an automatic script. Collect the MDM diagnostics first.
manualSteps: Collect diagnostics: mdmdiagnosticstool.exe -area "DeviceEnrollment;DeviceProvisioning;Autopilot" -cab C:\Temp\mdm.cab
Certificate missing or expired: delete the device in Intune, then enroll it again (see MDM.ENROLLMENT.MISSING)
More than one enrollment: compare the enrollment IDs in the MDM diagnostics; remove the orphaned one only with the diagnostics in hand
Certificate expires soon: it renews on a working sync, so fix MDM.SYNC.STALE first

fixes.title: Intune Management Extension missing or stopped
fixes.note: Starts the Intune Management Extension when it is stopped. A missing IME is not reinstalled: assign a PowerShell script or Win32 app to the device so Intune deploys it again.

fixes.title: Company Portal not installed
fixes.note: Installs Company Portal (9WZDNCRFJ3PZ) from the Microsoft Store with winget as SYSTEM. As an Intune remediation pair use Detect-CompanyPortalMissing.ps1 from the same folder as detection. Better long term: assign Company Portal as a required Microsoft Store app in Intune.

fixes.title: Company Portal damaged, hangs or sign-in fails
fixes.note: Resets Company Portal for the signed-in user (like Settings > Apps > Advanced options > Reset). Run it as the user, not as SYSTEM. The app stays installed and the enrollment is untouched; the user signs in to Company Portal again. Also helps when Company Portal shows a wrong compliance state or cannot install apps. If the package stays damaged, reinstall it (CP.APP.MISSING).

fixes.title: Entra join or Primary Refresh Token missing
fixes.note: Join and token problems depend on the identity setup, so they are guided steps. dsregcmd /status (as the user) shows the cause in its Diagnostic Data section.
manualSteps: Run dsregcmd /status as the signed-in user and check AzureAdJoined, DeviceAuthStatus, AzureAdPrt and the 'Attempt Status' and 'Server Error Code' lines
Not joined (cloud): Settings > Accounts > Access work or school > Connect > Join this device to Microsoft Entra ID
Not joined (hybrid): check that Entra Connect syncs the computer object, then run the task \Microsoft\Windows\Workplace Join\Automatic-Device-Join or dsregcmd /join as SYSTEM
DeviceAuthStatus FAILED: the device object is disabled or deleted in Entra ID; enable it, or rejoin the device
No PRT: lock and unlock or sign out and in again, then dsregcmd /refreshprt as the user; check time sync, access to login.microsoftonline.com and TPM health (tpm.msc)

fixes.title: Hybrid Entra join not completed
fixes.note: Enables the Automatic-Device-Join task and runs dsregcmd /join as SYSTEM, then reports the join error codes. The join only completes after Entra Connect has synced the computer object, so a first failure right after a new domain join is normal.
manualSteps: Run dsregcmd /status and read Error Phase, Client ErrorCode and Server ErrorCode in the Diagnostic Data section
Entra Connect: the computer OU must be in sync scope and the object needs a userCertificate value; check that the device appears in Entra ID with join type Hybrid
SCP: Entra Connect > Configure device options must have created the service connection point for your tenant
Network: the device needs access to enterpriseregistration.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com and device.login.microsoftonline.com as SYSTEM (proxy!)
Run as SYSTEM: dsregcmd /join, then sign out and in again

fixes.title: Device Entra joined and also Entra registered
fixes.note: The user added the work account as a registered account on top of the join. This can break Conditional Access, SSO and Intune enrollment. Registration is per user, so it is a guided step in the user context.
manualSteps: As the user: Settings > Accounts > Access work or school, disconnect the extra work account that is not the join
Or as the user: dsregcmd /cleanupaccounts, then sign out and in
Prevent it: set HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WorkplaceJoin BlockAADWorkplaceJoin = 1 (DWORD) through Intune or GPO
Check again with dsregcmd /status as the user: WorkplaceJoined must be NO

fixes.title: System clock wrong or Windows Time service disabled
fixes.note: Restores the default start type of W32Time, runs w32tm /resync /force and, only if the clock is still more than 5 minutes off, sets it once from the HTTPS Date header of login.microsoftonline.com. The time source configuration is not changed.

fixes.title: Defender antivirus or sensor service not running
fixes.note: Does nothing when another antivirus is active. Removes leftover DisableAntiSpyware/DisableAntiVirus Group Policy values (key backed up to C:\ProgramData\DefenderFix\Backup, skipped with a Configuration Manager client or -removePolicyBlocks 0) and starts WinDefend. ForceDefenderPassiveMode is only reported.
manualSteps: Get-MpComputerStatus
Check for third-party antivirus and tamper protection

fixes.title: Defender signatures older than 3 days
fixes.note: Runs MpCmdRun -SignatureUpdate from the configured source, then directly from Microsoft (-MMPC), then once more after clearing only the cached dynamic signatures. Update source settings are not changed.
manualSteps: "%ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender\MpCmdRun.exe" -SignatureUpdate

fixes.title: Real-time protection disabled
fixes.note: Reports an Intune policy that switches protection off, removes leftover Real-Time Protection Group Policy values (backed up first, skipped with a Configuration Manager client or -removePolicyBlocks 0) and resets the local Defender preferences. Tamper protection can only be turned on from Intune.
manualSteps: Get-MpComputerStatus
Check Intune endpoint security antivirus policy

fixes.title: Tamper protection off
fixes.note: No script can fix this: Windows only accepts tamper protection from Intune or the Defender portal, so that malware cannot switch it off either. Turn it on by policy.
manualSteps: Intune: Endpoint security > Antivirus > Create policy > Windows > Windows Security Experience > TamperProtection (Device) = On, assign to the device group
Or tenant-wide: Microsoft Defender portal > Settings > Endpoints > Advanced features > Tamper protection = On (needs Defender for Endpoint)
Check that no Intune or Group Policy setting turns real-time protection off, then sync the device

fixes.title: Defender for Endpoint not onboarded or not reporting
fixes.note: Installs the Sense capability when it is missing, checks that the Intune EDR onboarding policy has arrived, re-enables DiagTrack and starts Sense. Assign it only to devices that should be onboarded to Defender for Endpoint.
manualSteps: Check HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Advanced Threat Protection\Status OnboardingState
Run the MDE Client Analyzer

fixes.title: OS drive not encrypted or BitLocker waiting for activation
fixes.note: Turning on encryption must go through your BitLocker policy so the recovery key is escrowed first, so this is a guided step. The check detail shows the last BitLocker error event, which usually names the cause.
manualSteps: Read the last BitLocker error in the check detail (Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > BitLocker-API > Management)
Check that a disk encryption policy is assigned: Intune admin center > Endpoint security > Disk encryption, and the device status there
Silent encryption needs: a ready TPM (BL.TPM.NOTREADY), enabled WinRE (BL.WINRE.DISABLED), UEFI with Secure Boot, and no third-party encryption
Standard users: the policy must allow standard users to enable encryption during Entra join
"Waiting for activation" (encrypted, no protector): fixes itself once the policy applies; or run manage-bde -protectors -add C: -tpm, then BackupToAAD-BitLockerKeyProtector
After the fix: check the recovery key in Intune admin center > Devices > the device > Recovery keys

fixes.title: BitLocker protection suspended
fixes.note: Runs Resume-BitLocker on the OS drive. Only for an indefinite suspension; a suspension with a restart count resumes by itself. Do not run it while a BIOS/firmware update waits for its restart.

fixes.title: BitLocker recovery key not backed up to Entra ID
fixes.note: Adds a recovery password if none exists and backs up every recovery password to Entra ID. Harmless when the key is already there. Confirm afterwards in Intune admin center > Devices > the device > Recovery keys.

fixes.title: Windows Recovery Environment disabled
fixes.note: Runs reagentc /enable. Needed for silent BitLocker encryption, Autopilot reset and remote wipe. If it fails, Winre.wim is missing or the recovery partition is broken: see the steps.
manualSteps: reagentc /info shows the state; reagentc /enable turns it on
Winre.wim missing in C:\Windows\System32\Recovery: copy it from the install.wim of installation media with the same Windows build, then reagentc /enable
Recovery partition too small for WinRE updates: follow Microsoft KB5028997 (resize the partition), then reagentc /enable

fixes.title: TPM missing, not ready or only 1.2
fixes.note: TPM problems are fixed in the firmware or by the manufacturer, so this is a guided step. BitLocker, Windows Hello, the Entra device key and Autopilot depend on the TPM.
manualSteps: Open tpm.msc (or Get-Tpm as admin) and read the status and the recommended action
TPM not found: enable it in the BIOS/UEFI (Intel PTT, AMD fTPM or Security Chip)
Not ready: install the latest BIOS/UEFI and TPM firmware from the manufacturer, then check again
Clearing the TPM (tpm.msc > Clear TPM) is a last resort: suspend BitLocker first and make sure the recovery key is backed up, because Windows Hello keys and virtual smart cards are lost
TPM 1.2: Windows 11 and Autopilot pre-provisioning need 2.0; some models can be switched with a firmware tool from the manufacturer

fixes.title: Devices with driver problems
fixes.note: Rescans devices (pnputil /scan-devices) and installs the driver updates Windows Update offers for this device, then checks again. No driver is removed and no restart is forced. Devices that Windows Update has no driver for need the manufacturer driver (OEM tool or driver pack). For a guided choice of Windows, Office and driver updates there is Invoke-ManagedUpdates.ps1 in the TEST-TreiberUpdateScript repository.

fixes.title: Driver updates from Windows Update blocked by policy
fixes.note: Often intended (drivers from an OEM tool or ConfigMgr). If not, the policy must change where it is set, so this is a guided step.
manualSteps: Find the source: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate (GPO) or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\PolicyManager\current\device\Update (Intune)
Intune: Update ring > Windows drivers = Allow, or manage drivers with Windows Autopatch / Intune driver update policies
GPO: Windows Components > Windows Update > Do not include drivers with Windows Updates = Not configured
Co-managed with WSUS for drivers: move the Windows Update policies workload to Intune or approve drivers in WSUS
